propositions: Nested pytest child process can hang after reporting 100% completion when pytest session cleanup synchronously scans and deletes stale numbered temp trees in the user-global shared root.

Omitting --basetemp in the nested pytest invocation causes the child to join pytest's user-global numbered temp root instead of using a caller-owned private basetemp, violating store isolation invariants.

Private --basetemp parameter passed to nested pytest child with tmp_path/nested-pytest isolates session-finish cleanup and prevents unrelated temp directory retention from consuming the fixed 90-second timeout budget.
Controlled real-filesystem A/B test with 400,000 stale entries demonstrated cleanup cost scales with retained entries: shared-root baseline 10.800s versus private-basetemp 0.882s.
